title: Cap-set status and a sharp quadratic-graph dimension barrier
exact_target: Determine the maximum number of points in a vector space over the three-element field with no three on an affine line.
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $r\ge1$ and let $\mathbb F_3^r$ be the $r$-dimensional vector
space over the field of three elements. An affine line has the form
\[
                         \{x,x+d,x+2d\},\qquad d\ne0,
\]
with $x,d\in\mathbb F_3^r$. It has exactly three distinct points.
A cap set is a subset containing no such line. Since the
characteristic is three, this is equivalently the condition that
$x+y+z=0$ with $x,y,z\in A$ has no solution with three distinct
entries; any solution with two equal entries has all three equal.

Define
\[
 M(r)=\max\{|A|:A\subseteq\mathbb F_3^r,
                               A\text{ contains no affine line}\}.
\]
The problem asks for the largest possible cap-set size, as a function
of dimension, including sharp asymptotic estimates as $r\to\infty$.
The maximum is over arbitrary subsets, not just subspaces, graphs
of functions, or sets invariant under a specified symmetry group.
A fundamental asymptotic parameter is the exponential growth rate
$\sup_{r\ge1}M(r)^{1/r}$: Cartesian products of cap sets are cap
sets, so $M(r+s)\ge M(r)M(s)$ and the corresponding root limit
exists. Determining this rate is one precise aspect of determining
the growth of $M(r)$; it is weaker than an exact formula in every
dimension. Exponential upper bounds alone do not specify the optimal
rate or resolve the full extremal question posed by the workshop.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Determine the maximum number of points in a vector space over the three-element field with no three on an affine line.
